text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-Italy's entry to the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) can affect Swedish rates and its exchange rate when financial markets open on Monday. Speculation could grow that Sweden might soon follow the Italians, which would have the effect of sinking rates and strengthening the crown. Sweden, Greece and Britain are now the only European Union (EU) countries outside the currency grid, and this increases the political pressure on Sweden to go in.

-Proposals for the state pension funds (AP funds) to place more of their assets in listed companies need to be thoroughly investigated because of potentially negative effects. So far many industrial leaders, bourse commentators and insurance companies have greeted the proposals, but some voices are now being raised that the influx of assets could damage the supply of risk capital.

-Handelsbanken economist Jan Haggstrom did not see any immediate impact on Swedish rates from the Italian ERM re-entry. "We are not connected with the Italian decision. The pressure on Sweden to go in increases a bit but it has already been considerable," Haggstrom said. Handelsbanken's chief economist Carl B Hamilton said he thought the market would test the Italian lira, probably during 1997. "There will probably be a speculative attack against the lira and they will test which band rate Italy is prepared to defend," he said.

-Leftist Party member Johan Lonnroth said the Italian re-entry was not very significant for Sweden. "Possibly in the short-term rates in Sweden will rise. The crown will weaken, but that too in the short term," he said. The Leftist Party opposes Swedish entry to the ERM and EMU.

-Swedish Railways (SJ) will lower prices on several routes substantially next Spring, the state-owned company's director-general Stig Larsson said in an interview. He denied that the railways were in crisis. "No, we are financially strong. all right, we have problems but we can stick it out. And the rate of loss has actually fallen." He said the loss this year would be "more than 400 million" crowns.

-Pressure is going to mount on both the government and Riksbank, the central bank, to link the crown to ERM after the Italian re-entry. Sweden and Greece are now the only countries outside the grid and without an opt-out clause on EMU. Britain and Denmark have negotiated such an opt-out for themselves. The government and central bank is not too flattered at being in the company of Greece when they meet colleagues in the EU.
Especially when the government has pushed through such a thorough and in many cases impressive stabilisation of public finance.

-The Riksbank will probably lower its key repo rate on Tuesday by 0.2-0.3 percentage points. Expectations of this are based on the latest inflation statistics which show Sweden with falling consumer prices - deflation - together with other data indicating continued low pressure on inflation. Tomorrow the last reverse repurchase operation at a fixed 4.60 percent expires. Riksbank governor Urban Backstrom said when introducing the four-week fixed rate that economic statistics would determine whether or not there was room for further cuts in the key rate. -- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017
